**Henri**[[a]](#cite_note-2) ([French](/wiki/French_language "French language"): *Henri Albert Gabriel Félix Marie Guillaume*;[[2]](#cite_note-3) born 16 April 1955) is a member of the [grand ducal family of Luxembourg](/wiki/Grand_ducal_family_of_Luxembourg "Grand ducal family of Luxembourg") who reigned as [Grand Duke of Luxembourg](/wiki/Grand_Duke_of_Luxembourg "Grand Duke of Luxembourg") from 2000 until [his abdication](/wiki/Abdication_of_Henri,_Grand_Duke_of_Luxembourg "Abdication of Henri, Grand Duke of Luxembourg") in 2025.

Henri was born during the reign of his paternal grandmother, [Grand Duchess Charlotte](/wiki/Grand_Duchess_Charlotte "Grand Duchess Charlotte"), as the second child and eldest son of the future [Grand Duke Jean](/wiki/Grand_Duke_Jean "Grand Duke Jean") and [Princess Joséphine-Charlotte of Belgium](/wiki/Princess_Jos%C3%A9phine-Charlotte_of_Belgium "Princess Joséphine-Charlotte of Belgium"). He became [heir apparent](/wiki/Heir_apparent "Heir apparent") upon the accession of his father in 1964 at the age of nine, and was officially created [hereditary grand duke](/wiki/Hereditary_Grand_Duke_of_Luxembourg "Hereditary Grand Duke of Luxembourg") on his 18th birthday in 1973. Henri was educated in Luxembourg and [France](/wiki/France "France"), where he received his [Baccalauréat](/wiki/Baccalaur%C3%A9at "Baccalauréat") in 1974. He then undertook military officer training at the [Royal Military Academy Sandhurst](/wiki/Royal_Military_Academy_Sandhurst "Royal Military Academy Sandhurst"), on the Standard Military Course (SMC) 7, and then studied [political science](/wiki/Political_science "Political science") at [University of Geneva](/wiki/University_of_Geneva "University of Geneva") and the [Graduate Institute of International Studies](/wiki/Graduate_Institute_of_International_Studies "Graduate Institute of International Studies"), graduating in 1980.

The [Senate Judiciary Committee](/wiki/United_States_Senate_Committee_on_the_Judiciary "United States Senate Committee on the Judiciary") scheduled three or four days of public hearings on Kavanaugh's nomination, commencing on September 4, 2018. The hearings were delayed at the onset by objections from the Democratic members about the absence of records of Kavanaugh's time in the George W. Bush administration. The Democrats also complained that 42,000 pages of documents had been received only the night before the first day of hearings.[[166]](#cite_note-166) Republicans asserted that the volume of documents available on Kavanaugh equaled that of the previous five nominees to the court; the Democrats responded that only 15% of the documents they had requested about Kavanaugh had been provided. Numerous motions by the Democrats to adjourn or suspend the hearings were ruled out of order by Chairman [Chuck Grassley](/wiki/Chuck_Grassley "Chuck Grassley"), who argued that Kavanaugh had written over 300 legal opinions available for review. The first day's session closed after statements from each senator and the nominee, with question-and-answer periods to begin the next day.[[167]](#cite_note-167)

During the first round of questions from senators on September 5, 2018, Kavanaugh held to his earlier stated position that he would not express an opinion on matters that might come before the Court. He thus refused to promise to [recuse](/wiki/Judicial_disqualification "Judicial disqualification") himself from any case, including any that might involve Trump. He also declined to comment on coverage of preexisting healthcare conditions, semiautomatic rifle possession, *Roe v. Wade*, or the president's power to self-pardon. He expounded at length on various Constitutional amendments, [stare decisis](/wiki/Stare_decisis "Stare decisis") (the role of legal precedent in shaping subsequent judicial rulings), and the president's power to dismiss federal employees. Essential for the actual birth of the institutions of the EU was the [Schuman Declaration](/wiki/Schuman_Declaration "Schuman Declaration") on 9 May 1950 (the day after the fifth [Victory in Europe Day](/wiki/Victory_in_Europe_Day "Victory in Europe Day")) and the decision by six nations (France, Belgium, Netherlands, Luxembourg, West Germany, and Italy) to follow Schuman and draft the [Treaty of Paris](/wiki/Treaty_of_Paris_(1951) "Treaty of Paris (1951)"). This treaty was created in 1952 the [European Coal and Steel Community](/wiki/European_Coal_and_Steel_Community "European Coal and Steel Community") (ECSC), which was built on the [International Authority for the Ruhr](/wiki/International_Authority_for_the_Ruhr "International Authority for the Ruhr"), installed by the Western Allies in 1949 to regulate the coal and steel industries of the Ruhr area in West Germany.[[29]](#cite_note-35) Backed by the [Marshall Plan](/wiki/Marshall_Plan "Marshall Plan") with large funds coming from the United States since 1948, the ECSC became a milestone organisation, enabling European economic development and integration and being the origin of the main institutions of the EU such as the [European Commission](/wiki/European_Commission "European Commission") and [Parliament](/wiki/European_Parliament "European Parliament").[[30]](#cite_note-36)

After the trade of star [Wilt Chamberlain](/wiki/Wilt_Chamberlain "Wilt Chamberlain") in January 1965, the team finished the [1964–65 season](/wiki/1964%E2%80%9365_NBA_season "1964–65 NBA season") with the NBA's worst record (17–63). Their rebuilding period was brief, however, as they drafted [Rick Barry](/wiki/Rick_Barry "Rick Barry") four months after the trade. Barry, along with [Jamaal Wilkes](/wiki/Jamaal_Wilkes "Jamaal Wilkes"), powered the Warriors to their third championship in [1975](/wiki/1975_NBA_Finals "1975 NBA Finals"), widely considered one of the biggest upsets in NBA history.

The team struggled in the 1980s, then became playoff regulars at the turn of the decade with stars [Tim Hardaway](/wiki/Tim_Hardaway "Tim Hardaway"), [Mitch Richmond](/wiki/Mitch_Richmond "Mitch Richmond"), and [Chris Mullin](/wiki/Chris_Mullin "Chris Mullin"), nicknamed "[Run TMC](/wiki/Run_TMC "Run TMC")". Led by [Stephen Curry](/wiki/Stephen_Curry "Stephen Curry"), [Klay Thompson](/wiki/Klay_Thompson "Klay Thompson"), and [Draymond Green](/wiki/Draymond_Green "Draymond Green"), the team returned to championship glory in [2015](/wiki/2015_NBA_Finals "2015 NBA Finals"). At the same time, he opened negotiations with [Francis II, Holy Roman Emperor](/wiki/Francis_II,_Holy_Roman_Emperor "Francis II, Holy Roman Emperor"). Soon afterwards, at [Memel](/wiki/Klaip%C4%97da "Klaipėda"), he entered into a close alliance with [Prussia](/wiki/Prussia "Prussia"), not as he boasted from motives of policy, but in the spirit of true [chivalry](/wiki/Chivalry "Chivalry"), out of [friendship](/wiki/Friendship "Friendship") for the young King [Frederick William III of Prussia](/wiki/Frederick_William_III_of_Prussia "Frederick William III of Prussia") and his beautiful wife [Louise of Mecklenburg-Strelitz](/wiki/Louise_of_Mecklenburg-Strelitz "Louise of Mecklenburg-Strelitz").[[27]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPhillips1911557-29)

The development of this alliance was interrupted by the short-lived peace of October 1801, and for a while it seemed as though [France](/wiki/French_Consulate "French Consulate") and Russia might come to an understanding.
